scenario: A municipal archive will digitize exactly seven manuscripts—Gaelic, Hittite, Javanese, Kushite, Latin, Mongol, and Norse—one at a time, on seven consecutive workdays numbered 1 through 7. The digitization order must conform to the following conditions: Gaelic is digitized before Latin. Norse is digitized before Javanese. Kushite is digitized on a later day than Latin. Hittite is not digitized on day 1 and is not digitized on day 7. Mongol and Norse are not digitized on consecutive days. If Gaelic is digitized on day 2, then Hittite is digitized on day 4. If Javanese is digitized before Kushite, then Mongol is digitized on day 1.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true about the digitization order?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Kushite is digitized on day 5 or later.

explanations.correct: Gaelic < Latin < Kushite places at least two manuscripts before Kushite; Norse < Javanese places Javanese after Norse. With Hittite restricted to days 2–6, Kushite cannot be earlier than day 5 in any arrangement consistent with all six rules.
explanations.A: Gaelic could be on day 2 or 3 (e.g., Norse on day 1).
explanations.C: Javanese could be on day 5, 6, or 7 depending on placement of Mongol and Hittite.
explanations.D: Mongol could be on day 6 or 7, after Kushite.
explanations.E: Hittite can occupy day 3, 4, or 5 in various valid orderings.

questions.questionStem: If Norse is digitized on day 1, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: With Norse on day 1, Mongol cannot be on day 2 (non-adjacency). Gaelic-Latin-Kushite must occupy three days with Kushite late. Working through the remaining placements, Mongol is forced to day 7 in every valid world.
explanations.A: Gaelic can be on day 2 or day 3.
explanations.B: Hittite can be on day 4 or other middle days depending on Latin's placement.
explanations.D: Javanese can fall on day 2, 5, or 6.
explanations.E: Latin can be on day 3, 4, or 5.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: Kushite follows Gaelic and Latin, so at least two manuscripts precede it. Moreover Hittite cannot occupy day 1 or day 7, which further compresses the early days. No valid arrangement places Kushite earlier than day 5.
explanations.A: Gaelic on day 3 is realized in a valid ordering with Norse/Javanese on days 1/2.
explanations.B: Hittite on day 3 appears in multiple valid orderings.
explanations.C: Latin on day 2 occurs when Gaelic is on day 1.
explanations.E: Mongol on day 1 is possible with Gaelic on day 2.

questions.questionStem: If Javanese is digitized on day 2, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Javanese on day 2, Norse must occupy day 1. Gaelic, Latin, Kushite fill later days in order, Hittite takes an interior day, and Mongol must be on day 7 to avoid adjacency with Norse and to leave the early middle days for Gaelic/Latin/Hittite. This arrangement is realized in a valid world.
explanations.A: If Javanese is on day 2, Norse must be on day 1 (Norse before Javanese), so Gaelic cannot be on day 1.
explanations.B: Hittite cannot be on day 7 by the base rule.
explanations.C: Javanese is on day 2, so Latin cannot also be on day 2.
explanations.E: Kushite on day 3 would leave Latin only day 2 or earlier, but Javanese occupies day 2 and Gaelic must precede Latin—impossible.
